paper.title: Extreme high accuracy prediction and design of Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel using machine learning
paper.research_type: mixed (machine learning/computational modeling combined with experimental validation)
paper.paper_scope: Develops a data-driven model (SVR combined with firefly optimization and CGAN data augmentation, plus a modified solid solution strengthening theory) to predict and inversely design the microhardness of Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel; three designed alloys were then fabricated by arc cladding to validate the prediction accuracy.

unmapped_findings: The ML model was trained on 173 Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel data points collected from the MatWeb repository, covering 11 elements (C, Si, Mn, Cr, S, Ni, P, Fe, Mo, V, W) plus microhardness; after Z-score and isolation-forest outlier removal and CGAN augmentation the dataset was expanded from 98 to 192 data points, and 117 additional MatWeb data points served as a validation set.
The ASTM A36 steel plates (300 mm × 120 mm × 40 mm) were used only as cladding substrates, not as the studied alloy.

Inverse design optimized C, Si, Mn, Cr, S, Ni, P, Mo, V and W within given composition ranges using firefly optimization (FA), simulated annealing (SA), particle swarm optimization (PSO) and grey wolf optimization (GWO); FA yielded the highest predicted microhardness (733.59 HV), followed by PSO (730.04 HV), GWO (708.60 HV) and SA (700.37 HV).
The modified solid solution strengthening equation Δσsss = Z·M·G·δEc·DEc (Z = 0.0056, M = 3.06) was incorporated into the SVR model, raising R² from 0.85 to 0.89 and reducing RMSE from 0.39 to 0.31.
